build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The courier moves responsively with keyboard input in a top-down stealth level, with smooth multi-frame movement and collision that prevents passing through walls, doors, furniture, or the map edge. Score 0 if the courier is static, teleports, or ignores level boundaries.

At least two guards patrol autonomously along visible routes, reverse or turn at route endpoints, and continue without player input. Their bodies and facing directions are readable. Score 0 if guards are static, move randomly, or appear only as text labels.

Guard vision cones are visible, attached to guard facing direction, and update as guards patrol or turn. Entering a cone triggers a detection response with at least a warning state before capture. Staying outside cones avoids detection. Score 0 if cones are absent, detached from guard direction, or detection has no gameplay consequence.

The level contains a key or credential pickup and at least one locked door. Collecting the key visibly updates the HUD or inventory and allows passage through the locked route; without the key the door blocks progress. Score 0 if key state is invisible, the door is never actually locked, or pickup has no effect.

A light switch or shadow-control interaction changes the stealth state of the level: lights dim, guard cone range changes, or safe shadow areas expand. The change is visible in the environment and reflected in gameplay. Score 0 if the switch is cosmetic only or detection behavior is unaffected.

The playable map has an authored stealth layout with multiple rooms or zones, corridors, cover objects, walls, doors, a document objective, and an exit route arranged so patrol timing and route choice matter. Score 0 if the level is a single empty room or flat arena.

At least three distinct guard or security behaviors affect route choice -- such as fixed patrols, rotating sentries, widened alert cones, search movement after suspicion, cameras, or alarms. Score 0 if all threats behave identically.

The document theft is a real objective: the target is visible in the environment, interacting with it changes mission state, and the player cannot win until the document is stolen. Score 0 if the document is only mentioned in text, theft is automatic, or escape works before theft.

At least two stealth tools or environmental affordances besides basic movement are demonstrated -- such as hiding behind cover, crouch mode, noisemakers, disabling cameras, locking doors behind the player, light switches, vents, or shadow zones. Each has a visible gameplay effect. Score 0 if no tools exist or all are cosmetic.

The mission has both success and failure outcomes. Reaching the exit with the document triggers a styled success screen; being captured triggers a styled failure screen. Both halt gameplay and offer retry or return-to-title controls. Score 0 if either outcome is missing or allows gameplay to continue underneath.
A styled title screen shows the game name, a clear Start button, and a non-default covert background. Score 0 if the game starts directly in the level or uses raw default UI.

The full flow connects title -> briefing -> playable infiltration -> success or failure result -> retry or title without restarting the executable. Score 0 if any major transition is missing or broken.

During stealth gameplay the HUD is readable and non-overlapping at 1280x720, showing mission status such as key possession, document state, light/blackout state, alert level, and escape objective. Score 0 if core mission state is hidden or appears only as raw debug labels.

Stealth readability is strong: courier, guards, vision cones, walls, doors, cover, lights, key, document, and exit are distinguishable by silhouette, color, or iconography during normal play. Score 0 if the player cannot tell threats, objectives, and obstacles apart.

Overall art direction is coherent across title, briefing, map, courier, guards, lighting, cones, keys, document, HUD, and results. The game reads as a shadowy courier infiltration, not a collection of default controls. Score 0 if most visible elements are default shapes, raw ColorRects, or unthemed placeholders. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The stealth environment uses real sprite or tile art for walls, floors, doors, cover, and lighting -- not plain ColorRect fills or default HTML 引擎 primitives. Different map elements are visually distinct and recognisable. Score 0 if the environment is uniform color fills or unstyled rectangles.

HUD and UI chrome: mission panels, alert indicators, key/document icons, result screens, and menu buttons use styled themed widgets rather than raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled default widgets.

Animation and feedback are present: courier movement, guard patrols, cone sweeps, pickup effects, door unlock feedback, light transitions, detection escalation, and result transitions use smooth multi-frame animation or tweening. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently with no animation.
